incident_description: My 15 month old was playing with his PolarB Fishing Game by the brand Viga. He ran to me and handed me a small metal piece that fell off the fish that is used to attract the magnet in the fishing rod. If I wasnt close by he could have swallowed or choked on the piece if he didnt bring it to me immediately.
justification: The child could have swallowed or choked on the small metal piece, which poses a risk of injury or death.

incident_description: We obtained a motorized jeep with remote control. We had some concern that it could flip, so elected to have our children wear a helmet while riding. Our daughter was riding in the jeep while my husband was driving it via remote on our relatively flat driveway (there is a very slight incline). He was reversing the vehicle, stopped reversing to go forward. In doing this, the truck completed flipped backwards onto our child. Again, this was a very slight incline, we have a relatively flat driveway, so the momentum to flip came from the fact that the truck is heaviest in the back and the change in directions. Thankfully our daughter was not injured physical, just scared, likely due to our decision to have her wear a helmet while riding the truck.
justification: The child was not injured due to wearing a helmet, but the jeep flipped, which constitutes an incident.

incident_description: On March 18, [REDACTED] Station [REDACTED] Seattle Fire Department successsfully extricated a child who was stuck in a Tumble Forms 2 Barrel Crawl Roll--his lower body--of waist and of legs, of feet were bent in and tucked in this Roll's  center hole.  This child seemed stuck for over 5 minutes, we cut away over 10 % of the outer lining and we cut 2-4 inch long  sliver at its inner lining and then the inner lining seemed to expand and widen and the child sprung completely free of trapped in this Roll's hole.
justification: The child was stuck but successfully extricated without reported injury.

I strongly urge your team to investigate this product for potential safety violations.

incident_description: I purchased a set of mini silicone popsicle molds marketed under the brand "Angel of Mine" that are being sold for use with babies. I believe that they are unsafe and pose a legitimate choking hazard . I purchased them from my local Dollar Tree store. The item in question is Distributed by Greenbriar International Inc. , [REDACTED], Chesapeake, VA 23320. The labeling indicates that the item was manufactured in China. The parts include a one piece silicone mold with four "wells"(roughly an inch deep) to fill with juice, fruit, baby food (specifically mentioned on packaging), before freezing. Included are four plastic, stick like handles (approximately 3 inches long by 3/4 of an inch wide at the widest point, and  thickness that varies from 1/8th of an inch to 5/16th of an inch thick at the thickest point of the stick) and caps for each well. The handles are meant to click securely into slots in the caps and then the assembled cap/stick are to be placed into the food or liquid to be placed in the freezer and be frozen to create a very small popsicle that can be eaten by a baby. Unfortunately, THE STICK PORTION DOES NOT CLICK FIRMLY INTO THE CAP and can come detached fairly easily, posing a choking hazard for a small baby or toddler as there is nothing to prevent the child from ingesting the stick/handle if and/or when it becomes detached. These mini popsicle molds are found in the area of the store specifically stocking baby feeding/care items and the "Angel of Mine" branding is also used exclusively on baby products within the store. No injuries occurred as the product is being used in a home with no children. My concern is that this item is being marketed for very small children and there is also no safety warning present on the box.
justification: The product poses a choking hazard for small children, but no injuries have occurred as it is not being used by children.

incident_description: I purchased a double stroller for my daughter who informed me that the buckle on child restraint of stroller does not engage properly and can be unfastened by infants.
justification: The buckle not engaging properly poses a potential risk of infants unfastening themselves, but no actual incident or injury has been reported.

incident_description: I purchased the Nickelodeon Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Rippin Rider Pogo Stick for my daughter as a Christmas gift.  She put on her knee pads and helmet and went out onto the driveway to jump.  Our driveway is flat and it was a dry, mild temperature day (about 58 deg).  She jumped twice and then proceeded to jump continuously, only making it to 30 jumps before the bolts and spring liberated and the bottom metal piece fell out.  Thank God for her helmet and knee pads, or she could have been seriously injured.  My daughter is 7 and weighs 68lb.  The product states that it is for children 5-9 and 40-80lb.  There is no explanation for why the pogo stick fell apart in under 2 minutes during the first use.  This toy is a safety hazard and I would like to warn other parents, so that they choose a different product if they are interested in purchasing a pogo stick for their child.
justification: The pogo stick failed during first use, but no injury occurred due to protective gear.

incident_description: Disney shell necklace battery compartment popped open. Screw does not close compartment and button batteries popped out.
justification: The battery compartment opening is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential hazard.

incident_description:
We experienced three instances of the Bugaboo Dragonfly stroller's seat collapsing with our baby daughter in it after unfolding the stroller. In all instances, the seat back collapsed downward after being unfolded with the seat in parent-facing mode. In one instance, the seat back collapsed so far that our daughter was angled towards the floor and began sliding towards the floor - a very scary potential of falling on her head/neck to the floor. We luckily were able to catch her before she fell, but barely. We immediately notified Bugaboo support and have yet to receive any response, which we think is irresponsible. Through a web search, we found this Bugaboo article: https://service.bugaboo.com/s/article/UPDATE-Important-notice-regarding-Bugaboo-Dragonfly-seat-safety?language=en_GB
The issue reporting instructions in that article are wrong (they point to a UK support email address), and the blame-y wording points to incorrect use by users. However, article doesn't describe how to unfold the stroller properly, and it is telling that it does not link directly to the user guide. In fact, the user guide is unreadable and unclear (literally - it includes pictures only, with no words!). We would like Bugaboo to (1) be clear about how to use its stroller safely and (2) immediately recall the unsafe stroller seat and replace it for all customers.
justification: The seat collapsing incidents could have led to injury but did not in these cases, and the issue has occurred multiple times with the same stroller.

incident_description: Stroller chassis unlocks while pushing and can close on a child while the child is in it. I have reached out to silver cross to address this issue and they are unable to provide any help as there is no "Official recall" in place and they do not care about the safety of the children. only until enough of them are injured or worse.
justification: The description implies potential for injury or death due to the stroller malfunction, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: Toy bought for grandchild. A part broke off the third time he played with it, revealing a sharp screw.
justification: A part broke off revealing a sharp screw, posing a potential hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: purchased happy meal w/toy. My 5 year old daughter was putting the stand together (it came in 3 pieces and you slide the pieces together). while she was putting 2 of the pieces together, she got the portion between her thumb and index finger caught in-between the 2 pieces.  This caused a blood blister on her hand

incident_description: Our 1 year olds received the following musical instrument set for Christmas.  Within a day,  one item, apparently called a "Bolang Gu" broke apart and left a very sharp thumb tack like item detached from the instrument.  Our twins easily could have put this in their mouth.  We are very concerned it could happen to other children.  There were two thumb tacks on the instrument, and while this one fell out very easily, the other is attached very securely.
justification: The incident involved a broken musical instrument with a sharp object that could have caused injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: My daughter wanted to accompany me on a run, not the first time but rather a habit. I proceeded to check the tire pressure and fill up the tires to the recommended PSI and check the hardware and straps to ensure everything was in working order and safe for both of us. We were well on our way and a mile into the run the front wheel  shook for a monment then the next moment I fell forward due to the stroller wheel coming out of place and my child was  face down in the stroller, on the ground. We both where horrified and as a parent I lost any confidence that BobJ Jogging stroller was a trusted product to have my child in. I expected more from a highe end stroller and now face a long road ahead as a military member of not being able to use a vital tool for the maintaining of mandatory level of acceptable fitness. Thank you for fielding my concerns
justification: The incident resulted in the child being face down in the stroller, indicating potential injury, and the parent was also affected by the fall.

incident_description:
I was walking my 13 month old baby in my Bob Revolution stroller (Model Number ST1024; manufacture date 01-22-2013).

I stepped slightly wrong on my right foot and lightly gripped the stroller handle for balance.  Suddenly, and without warning, the stroller accelerated downward.  I landed very hard on my right knee and right ankle.  The stroller completely flipped over and my baby was hanging upside down.  There is no way to prevent this because of the design of the stroller.  Even if I had let the stroller go (which would have been dangerous for my baby) there is a wrist band that you are required to wear which pulls the stroller over.

I went to the emergency room and got X-rays, pain medication, an [REDACTED] bandage, a boot and crutches.  One week later (today), I am still in pain. My right knee cap also hurts and my right knee is bruised and scraped.  In addition, my left knee and left hand are scraped.  I have an appointment with an orthopedist tomorrow.

In addition to the physical injuries, it was very emotionally upsetting to see my baby hanging upside down and in danger.

The company has knowledge that the stroller is at risk of tipping over, but still puts it on the market.
justification: The incident resulted in physical injuries requiring medical attention and emotional distress, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I previously purchased a Bright Starts Hop Along Carrier Toy Bar for my son to attach to his infant carrier. He has outgrown his infant car seat at 14 months and still likes to play with the toy. Thursday evening on July 19, 2012, he was playing with the toy (not attached to the car seat) and the back screw on battery cover plate came off. He ingested one of the 3 1.6 volt button batteries required to run the toy. At the time of the incident, the back cover plate was secured by one short metal screw that came with the toy. The screw was still threaded through the back cover plate but the screw and cover plate had come off of the toy exposing the batteries.
justification: The child ingested a button battery, which poses a serious injury risk.

incident_description: I have a jeep stroller that blew a inner tube resulting in the rim breaking and flying off. My child was next to the stroller as I was moving it and was injured in the incident. He received a laceration on the side of his abdomen as a result. I found out after the fact that these strollers have been recalled although my manufacture date was not included, even though the exact same thing happened to mine.
justification: The child received a laceration, indicating an injury, and the stroller's history of recalls suggests a possible recurrence.

incident_description: A male toddler aged approximately 17 months ingested a family member's Bupropion medication at his home.  He was taken to a local emergency department where he died.  The medical examiner's office performed an autopsy and toxicology studies.  The certified cause of death was "Acute Bupropion Intoxication."  The manner of death was "Accident."
justification: The incident resulted in the death of the toddler due to accidental ingestion of medication.

incident_description: FORT play couches (a childrens toy) are being shipped to consumers with loose magnets approximately the size of a quarter within the zippered covers.  The zipper is easily opened by a child leaving them subject to finding the loose magnets and placing them in their mouths which is a choking hazard at the very least and a situation that could be fatal should a child swallow more than one causing them to attract to each other within the childs body.  The company is offering no solution to the problem besides removing the magnets and placing them on your fridge.  The magnets were advertised as being sewn completely shut in the covers and were changed some time during production with no warning to consumers.  There is also no warning label or information sheet that accompanies this toy letting consumers know that it even contains magnets at all.  Nor does this product carry any kind of bar code that should be present according to the CSPC for childrens toys/furniture.  The only safety notation on the tag is that it passed the fire safety for furniture.  I believe this toy is extremely hazardous and an accident waiting to happen.  The owner will not reply to emails or provide adequate solutions.
justification: The presence of loose magnets poses a choking hazard and potential fatal internal injuries if swallowed, with no warnings or adequate safety measures provided.

incident_description: I am furious while writing this. I have the Baby Jogger City Mini GT2 Double Stroller, Slate. We purchased this stroller October 2020. I have a 14 month old daughter and a two month old son. I did my research and wanted to get the best, SAFEST stroller for my babies. Upon getting the stroller, I found out that my car seat did not fit into the stroller, but I loved the stroller so much that I went out and purchased a brand new car seat that would work and that was safe. I purchased numerous parts only for the parts to come and find out they didnt fit my new model of the double stroller. After a long hall, I purchased the [REDACTED] car seat, which then led me to purchase the car seat adapter. I also purchased 2 childs trays, a belly bar double and a parent console. Needless to say, I am well at a $1000 mark with all of the accessories etc. Still, I was happy to do it to have one of the best strollers for the kids. It wasnt until today that I found out how DANGEROUS this stroller is. Walking home from a neighbors house with both babies, my 14 month old started crying. I had the flap open on top and I looked down and thought she was just laying back. I figured she was fussing because she was tired. She started screaming. I then stopped immediately, went to get her out and realized her head was stuck, wedged in between the bar in the middle of the stroller and the seat. I HAD TO PRY MY CHILDS HEAD FROM THE BAR! This is unacceptable and I am mortified. I cannot believe, after all of the headaches of purchasing MULTIPLE things to make this stroller what I need it to be, it turns out its not safe at all.
justification: The incident describes a situation where a child's head was stuck in the stroller, requiring prying to free her, indicating potential injury.

Actually I originally bought it for my nephew as a gift. However, its smelly (like plastic) and I think maybe it is harmful for the children. Because it's so pungent that I feel dizzy and strange after I opened the package.  Therefore, Ive tried to contact the manufacturer to reflect this problem. Also, I think this product should be removed to prevent further potential risk brought by this product.

incident_description:
The parents of the victim placed their six month 18 pound son into the stroller. He was not seat belted in and was placed on top of a blanket on his stomach. The seat was placed in the recline position. They walked away for approximately 30-45 minutes. 

They then noticed that the infant had some how slid down to the bottom of the stroller and was face down with his face trapped in between the seat. The back of his head was against the tray and his face was pushed into the loge of he seat. His legs did not touch the ground.  The infant was not breathing and the amount of time he was in that position is unknown. 

The Fire Department was contacted and they were the first to arrive on the scene. They began performing CPR on the infant and were able to get a faint pulse. He was then rushed via EMT to *** in where they continued to work on him. They were not able to save his life and pronounced him dead. 

The Medical Examiner stated that the cause of death was due to Mechanical Asphyxiation. The Consumer in which filled the report later learned that the stroller in which was purchased a Yard sale/garage sale was affected by a recall See Release #11-015).
justification: The infant died due to mechanical asphyxiation caused by improper use of a recalled stroller.

incident_description:
A 2 year old deceased child came into the New Mexico Office of the Medical Investigator. Initial information
indicated she had choked on a piece of food, but during autopsy we located a small part of a toy in the child's
bronchus, specifically a small plastic pacifier. The toy is manufactured by Calico Toys and is part of a toy line called
"Critters" and is part of the Yellow Labrador Twins set within this toy line.

It is unknown how the child was playing with the toy at the time of her choking.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to choking on a toy part, indicating the highest severity level.

justification: The infant was found cold and stiff, indicating death, and the lack of buckling increases the likelihood of such incidents.

bruin drum of instruments. My 3 year old daughter was playing the trumpet that comes with the set and the small mouth piece came off IN her mouth!! Thankfully she was okay and took it out of her mouth, but if she had been inhaling or if she was a younger child, she could have easily choked!
Being the "Crafty" mom that I am, I tried to glue it back in, but it still detaches easily!
justification: The small mouthpiece came off in the child's mouth but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as the mouthpiece detaches easily.

incident_description: My children and I were home. I was watching television, and my children were playing. My daughter was playing with her toy baby stroller  a childs toy purchased from Sams East, Inc. (designed/manufactured by Defendant Lissi). In a moment, I heard my young daughter scream out  I turned to look at her  and then I saw my daughter pulling a metal rod from her rectum. The rod was the toy baby strollers axle. Immediately, my daughter began holding her stomach, showed her pain, and began moaning in pain. I responded by loading up both children in my vehicle, and driving directly to a Fire Station house near by. Upon arriving at the Fire Station, I was honking the horn, yelling, and surrendered my daughter  to the medics / paramedics. We then rushed to the Childrens Hospital to meet my daughter. Our 4 year old daughter did not survive her injuries and passed away that day.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to a toy-related injury, which is a severe outcome.

incident_description:
We opened the "Baby Einstein Musical Mix N Roll 4-in-1 Push Walker, Activity Center, Toddler Table and Floor Toy for 6 months+" and tried to lock it into the push walker mode. The latches would not lock, however. If you allowed a child to use it, thinking it was locked or thinking the lock was unnecessary, it would fold out into table mode but with no support on the other side leading a child to faceplant into the toy. 

No injuries occurred because we did not allow our foster children to use the toy in the push walker mode.
justification: No injuries occurred as the toy was not used in the faulty mode, but the potential for injury was present.

incident_description: I bought 2 products from Warmies, which sells heatable stuffed animals marketed to children.  We have used the product as intended.  Since we began using it in December 2022, the flaxseeds that are inside (they heat up upon microwaving to create a heating pad stuffed animal) have been working their way out.  They are not, apparently, in a thick enough or properly secured bag and the sharp ends of the seeds are pushing themselves out of the stuffed animals.  I have a friend who bought a Warmie shortly after I did since she liked the idea and she has also experienced a high volume of seeds working their way out even though she has had the product less than 2 months.  The seeds are quite sharp (and the child using the stuffed animal is obviously holding it close to their skin) and more importantly, are a major choking hazard for children, to whom the product is marketed.  I contacted the company and did not receive any sort of assurance regarding quality controls or safety nor did they do anything to indicate that they would investigate manufacturing practices to make sure this stops happening.
justification: The incident involves a product defect posing a choking hazard and potential injury risk to children, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: VapeL1FE, 861 US-1, Edison, NJ 08817, (732) 243-9617, support@vapel1fe.com, Copyright © 2019, VapeL1FE. Design by Jai Haze (legal name: [REDACTED]), registered with the New Jersey Secretary of State As a LLC, in the name of [REDACTED] (owner/operator). All the e liquid bottles are mostly in glass and do not have flow restrictors in accordance with Title 16, 1700.15(d) (most of the products sold have a manufactured finished product date post-August 8, 2016, this is rather a Food and Drug Administration matter). I have purchased in the past the e liquid entitled "Jai Haze Jimmy-Jo" https://vapel1fe.com/products/jai-haze-jimmy-jo (glass bottles) and "Jai Haze Triple" https://vapel1fe.com/products/jai-haze (glass bottles) which arrived in a bottle without the flow restrictor. Of course Vapel1fe/[REDACTED] had a legal duty to report his non-flow restrictor bottles as a retailer to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission ("CPSC"), but he failed to do so as CPSC Commissioner [REDACTED] stated on his Twitter page that 100% of the e liquid manufacturers/retailers have non-flow restrictors or are in violation of Title 16, 1700.15(d). If a child gets a hold of one of these non-flow restrictor bottles that [REDACTED] sells, a child may very well die like the child in December 2014 [REDACTED] "Police reported that the 1-year-old child died after ingesting liquid nicotine at a home in [REDACTED], on Tuesday. The child was found unresponsive and rushed to a hospital where he was later pronounced dead. One teaspoon of liquid nicotine could be lethal to a child, and smaller amounts can cause severe illness, often requiring trips to the emergency department". At that time, the Child Nicotine Poisoning Prevention Act was not yet law until January 28, 2016, nevertheless, the flow restrictors have been a statute (Title 16, 1700.15(d) well before December 2014. There was also another child death in Korea in December 2016 caused by e liquid nicotine poisoning: [REDACTED]   Must consumers ignore such matters until it's too late that another child dies? I agree with Commissioner [REDACTED] (and U.S. Senator [REDACTED]), now is the time to enforce, not wait until another child's death. There is no excuse for a e liquid manufacturer or retailer to wait for fatality to occur to realize these particular non-flow restrictor bottles need to be removed from the U.S. markets and its territories. A manufacturer or retailer should prompt the recall of these non-flow restrictor bottles voluntarily without having  a consumer like myself initiate the process to do so. (Please note: the dates that I purchased both e liquid bottles are not exact, could have been in the latter part of 2017 or early part of 2018)
justification: The description highlights a potential risk of child death due to ingestion of liquid nicotine from non-flow restrictor bottles, referencing past fatalities.

incident_description: I work in a large hospital based child care center. We own four of the six seater Bye Bye Buggies that are made by angeles. We take the children in our Infant/Toddler program for walks on the buggies every day. We frequently have to order replacement straps for the buggies. The most recent design of the straps has a 5- point harness with a release button in the middle. This button is very small and pops loose on a regular basis. This is a dangerous choking hazard since the buggies are for children 6 months and up. It also traps the child in the harness until we cut the straps or find a way to loosen the straps enough to work them free. I have tried contacting the manufacturer of the straps which I believe is Children's Factory. The product number is APL270BLK Seat Belt Replacement. This is an ongoing problem with all the straps but the most recent incident is the date I entered below.
justification: The straps pose a choking hazard and trap children, but no injury is reported in the description.

incident_description: On July 4, 2018 mom put both children (twins) into separate car seats to take a nap at a friend's house.  Mom recalls buckling both the chest strap and bottom buckle for both children prior to leaving the room.  The victim was later found unresponsive by a friend and declared deceased.  Friend reports bottom buckle was undone when she was found, and it appeared that she wiggled down to where the chest strap was under her neck.  On autopsy, the ME found no signs of trauma and reported that it appeared that the victim died form Asphyxiation due to compression of the neck.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to asphyxiation from improper car seat use.

incident_description: Graco FastAction Fold Jogger Click Connect Stroller - the main edge of the stroller split apart so it is no longer safe to put a child in it. I noticed it when folding it up.
justification: The stroller's structural failure poses a risk of injury if used, but no injury was reported in this incident.

incident_description:
I have bought this doll from Amazon for my daughter's first birthday: Kathe Kruse Waldorf Schatzi Plush Doll, Red (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B002KE1PR6/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1). Item model number 38202. The company's website: http://www.kathekruse-usa.com/play-dolls/waldorf-dolls/red-waldorf-sweetheart-doll.html

Within 15 min, my 1 year old pulled the feet off and started to chew them. The filling was also coming out. If I was not there, she could have choked and died. The feet alone are choking size for any human, let alone an infant. The wool (or whatever filling the doll has that was coming out) is also a choking hazard. I have searched for two months to find a good doll. My main criterion was safety (for example, avoiding products that are made in China, which comprises more than 99% of the market, including the Corrole dolls which cleverly give you the impression in the description that they are made in France, but ultimately it is still China). This doll met all my criteria (cotton, wool, meets requirements of US CPSIA, European EN71, recommended for infant).
justification: The doll's parts posed a choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred as the parent intervened in time.

incident_description: Today 3/5/14 I went to change the batteries in the soothe and glow seahorse it it was all rotted inside. We use this toy for my babies all the time! Something serious could have happened at anytime while this was laying in the crib with the baby. I don't know why these are not being recalled.
justification: The toy was rotted inside, posing a potential hazard, but no actual incident or injury occurred.

incident_description: A child was rocking back and forth on our Motion Play Spring Mates Pony in our pre-school play yard when the spring broke.  The child and horse fell to the side.  The child was not seriously injured but may have been and now all the Motion Play Spring toys on our play yard are suspect.
justification: The child was not seriously injured, but the incident could have resulted in injury, and other similar toys are now suspect.

incident_description: We bought one blister card of 'Robot Fish' from Hong Kong Toy R Us, before we open it, I found the attached button cell battery LR44 is serious gassing deformed, probably Explosion on behind, perhaps it may cause Eyes injury, please share to consumer !!
justification: The battery is deformed and gassing, posing a potential risk of explosion and eye injury, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
-We bought the stroller understanding, as the sales representatives at Albee Baby told us and as the Peg Perego website itself mentions, that each seat in the stroller is safe for a child up to fifty pounds. Our twins are 2 years old and each weigh about 28 pounds. 
-We received and assembled the stroller on Wednesday night, May 11, and started using it on the morning of Thursday, May 12. Immediately upon using it during that first week, my husband, my babysitter, and I all remarked how, when using the stroller, we all felt like it was going to tip over even when walking on a flat sidewalk and we were all a little hesitant about using the stroller. 
-On Saturday afternoon, March 21  less than 10 days after receiving the stroller  I was walking back with the twins and my parents from a playground near our home. We crossed a crosswalk, and continued along a sidewalk. About five steps later, as we were walking along the sidewalk, the stroller tipped completely towards my right side. It almost hit the ground, but my father and I were able to catch it when it was a few inches away from a complete hit. Upon putting the stroller upright, we noticed that the 5-point harness on my daughter, who was sitting in the upper seat, had come partially undone from the force of the fall. No injuries occurred, thankfully.
justification: The stroller tipped but was caught before hitting the ground, and no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer was handling the toy book for her granddaughter and was pricked on her right middle finger.  There was no injury, but the she was extremely concerned because there was an approximately 1 long (or longer) sewing needle inside the fabric, which protruded from the toy. 

3/2/2018:  The consumer called the manufacturer (Tel:  800-521-2010) and reported the incident to a rep.  the rep. apologized and said sometimes these things happen.  The rep. told the consumer that she could pick a replacement toy of her choice up to the value of this toy and they would send it to her free of charge.  The consumer declined the offer, because her purpose was to provide safety hazard information to the firm.
 
The consumers granddaughter has been playing with this toy for the past 3 months and has not sustained any injuries.  The consumer discontinued the childs use of the toy.

The toy does not appear to be included in any recalls.
justification: The consumer was pricked but sustained no injury, and the granddaughter had no injuries despite prolonged use.

incident_description:
While the 8 year old was playing with the cap gun (amount of time is unknown) , the roll of caps caught fire and fell to the floor. The cap gun spewed sparks in all directions.

The mother of the child was able to put the fire out (method was not provided). The toy was taken away from the child and the firm as not contacted because the consumer was not sure the name of the company.

No further information was provided.
justification: The incident involved a fire and sparks but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We found a sewing needle in the front foot of a large Beanie Boos Reagan purchased from Claire's in Wenatchee, Washington.  Oddly enough, we have had the stuffed animal for almost 2 months, but tonight, our daughter was sitting with the toy, and when she moved the toy to my wife's side, the needle stuck my wife.  I then took the toy and found the needle.  It is a sewing needle, unbroken.
justification: The needle caused an injury to the wife, but no further harm was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased the Banzai Soak and Splash Balls last night at my local Family Dollar Store in Machias, Maine.  When I got home I opened up the balls.  I was just about to hand them over to my two-year old daughter when I noticed a string.  I pulled the string and out came a sewing needle attached to this string.  I was mortified.  What if I hadn't seen the string and pulled out the needle?  Well, then my daughter would have had a sewing needle go straight into her hand.  The string attached to the needle was the same kind of thread used to sew the balls with.  To a mom, this is pretty scary stuff.

I then went online immediately to find a customer service phone number.  I called it and it told me that customer service was not open at the time.  So today I have attempted 5 separate times to get through customer service.  Each time they told me that all customer service workers were busy and I would have to wait until the next available worker.  Well, I did this each time and after just over 10 minutes my phone call got disconnected.  

So not only am I mortified about finding a sewing needle in a toy, I am very frustrated that I have spent well over a hour trying to get through the company's customer service.
justification: A sewing needle was found in a toy, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My 3 year old received a brand new Roadmaster red 12" tricycle for christmas (december 2014).  When we put it together, we noticed a strong chemical odor that was nauseating.  We left the tricycle outside for the past 3 months and then put it in our vehicle to move it to our house.  After the tricycle was sitting in our vehicle for 2 hours, we opened up the door and noticed a very strong odor.  We have continued to leave the tricycle outside, but still notice the strong chemical odor coming off of the tricycle.
justification: The strong chemical odor indicates a potential hazard, but no injury or health effects are reported.

incident_description:
On July 2, 2023, I purchased the GB Pockit Air All-Terrain stroller from Amazon.com for $199.95. Today, I went to use it with my one-year old daughter and despite following the instructions and hearing the stroller click open and lock, it collapsed, she fell backwards, and hit her head. There was nothing on the back of the stroller to protect her head from the concrete. Thankfully, my daughter does not appear injured at this time, but this was an alarming incident, caused a lot of tears, and I never want to use this product again. I also want other parents to be warned about this apparent design flaw. A stroller should not collapse downwards causing a child to fall and hit their head under any circumstances.

I went on the manufacturer's website to report the incident. Their online form requires an item number/serial number. The instructions say this should appear on the frame of the product. My product is not marked with a visible item number/serial number, so I have no mechanism of contacting the manufacture directly. I want a full refund of my purchase price. I also want the manufacturer to put a clear and unmistakable warning on the product, warning parents of the potential fall risk.
justification: The stroller collapsed causing the child to fall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: After having the Fisher-Price Soothe & Glow Seahorse, Pink for approximately one year, it suddenly began smoking one night. Luckily our very verbal daughter yelled "Mama" because when we came in her room is smelled like something was on fire. Sure enough the battery pack was burning. We held on to the toy and it is still brown and scorched where the burning occurred.
justification: The toy began smoking and burning, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While my 3 year old was wearing a pair of these dress up shoes, one shoe's insole broke into extremely sharp shards of harsh plastic under her bare foot. Thankfully she was not harmed, but it seems to be a hazard. I have saved the shoe, and can provide picture if needed.
justification: The shoe's insole broke into sharp shards, posing a hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My 5 year old son was playing with a character that was included with a set of magnetic tiles. (PicassoTiles Haunted House Theme Magnet Tile Building Blocks 8 Action Figures Magnetic Construction Toy Double Sided Printing) 

https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CKH243M5?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title

The characters have magnets in their feet that attach to the magnetic tiles. The foot came off the character and the small magnet that was in the foot came out. We can't find the magnet. These small magnets can be fatal to children and animals.
justification: The magnet came loose but no injury occurred, though there is a potential hazard.

incident_description: Baby trend Product #CS31711- FlexLoc. Chest Clip broke. Only normal wear and tear. Seat has never been in an accident and was purchased in September of 2014...
justification: The chest clip broke due to normal wear and tear, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My child may have permanent hearing damage, will be having her hearing tested. A toy phone volume is dangerously high, 118.2dB was the max and 102 was the average. The volume control is not child proof so even if you turn it low a child can turn it back higher. My ear hurts hours later, I cant image what it feels like to a child. The packaging is also false advertisement, in bold font it says 18m+ but the fine print on back says not for children 0-3 years. Both can not be correct and regardless there is no reason for a small childs toy to ever have the capacity to get this loud. What child wont what to put a phone to their ear during pretend play. A warning that was covered by the barcode. Children are fast, their should not be a toy that if you arent quick enough to pull away from their ear permanent damage is the risk.
justification: The toy phone's dangerously high volume and lack of child-proofing pose a risk of permanent hearing damage to children, as evidenced by the parent's reported ear pain and the child's upcoming hearing test.

incident_description: I have owned the Joovy Caboose Stand-On Tandem stroller for approx. 5 months. I have only used the child restraint belt about 5 times because I have mostly used the stroller with the infant car seat carrier. Three days ago I was going to strap my son in the seat for a walk and the left side of the buckle would not lock in place. I moved the male ends of the buckle a little and it eventually locked in place, but I was able to unlock it simply by pulling up on it.
justification: The buckle malfunctioned but did not result in injury, though it could pose a risk if not addressed.

incident_description:
I purchased a Baby Trend Expedition LX Jogging Stroller  Gracie from
Babies R Us in April 2012.  I was very satisfied with this stroller;
at first it was very stable. However, within a few months of purchase
it is wobbly and unstable.

On July 6th 2012, my daughter who is 19 months old was hurt by this
product.  While walking with the stroller her arm was badly pinched
and bruised.   Her arm was caught in between the left side of the
rail, where the top portion connects with the bottom portion of the
stroller just below the handle bar.  This was one of many times her
arm was pinched, but enough is enough.  The Baby Trend Expedition LX
Jogging Stroller  Gracie is wobbly and dangerous. I will be returning
it to Babies R Us.  Baby Trend products need to be safe for children.
Something should to be done to prevent this type of incident from
happening again.  No child should be hurt by the stroller.
justification: The child's arm was badly pinched and bruised, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: On January 16, 2012 my five year old girl lost her balance while sitting on the arm of our couch in our play area. She landed on my son's WWE crash down wrestling wring. The overhead of the wring gave way,however the corner post did not. All though all three turn buckles snapped off the cornerpost the post did not collapse. Instead it injured my daughter. She spent approximatly two weeks at CHOP after being rushed there for emergency surgery. The injuries are severe and were life threatening. The post perforated her rectum and vagina. After an agonizing two weeks in the hospital she is now home with a colostomy. We hope that in a few months she heals enough to have another surgery to reverse the colostomy. The physical, as well as, mental implications of this injury will not be fully realized. She may have life long issues as a result of this injury. My question is why didn't the post collapse or have some sort of break away feature. We also question the fact that there were absolutely NO warnings on the box or instructions concerning the POSTS and or injuries that may occur. The wring was on the floor. I'm sure that in most homes across America this is exactly were children play with this toy, on the floor. Feel free to call me at [REDACTED] with any questions. [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in severe, life-threatening injuries requiring emergency surgery and a colostomy, with potential lifelong physical and mental implications.

incident_description: My son received this as a gift for his 5th birthday.  While putting a [REDACTED] 9V battery in the remote control (it was new & right out of the box), which is what it required, the remote control started sparking and smoking! Dangerous toy!! I'm so glad my son wasn't the one putting the battery in! I saw that someone else had the same complaint and the manufacturer tried to say this was improper battery installation. I can assure you it was not. It was a 9V alkaline battery entered with proper polarity and obviously not mixed with other types of batteries as it just took one battery. My husband is a mechanic and we are intelligent enough to know how to properly install a battery in a child's toy.  I also read several Amazon reviews stating people have issues with parts flying off when using it. This toy should be recalled until these things can be corrected before someone gets hurt.
justification: The incident involved sparking and smoking but no injury occurred, and similar complaints suggest a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
Want to report the following product that caught on fire as my kid was riding it. It burnt a big hole on the seat above the battery.

Joyracer 4WD 24V Ride on Toys UTV with Remote Control, 2 Seater Ride on Dump Truck, 4x200W Electric Powered 4-Wheeler Toys with Trailer & Shovel, MP3/[REDACTED] Music, Big Kids, Green
Actual Color: Green
Qty 1
New
$240.00 from savings

sold by walmart.
justification: The product caught fire, causing damage but no reported injury.

incident_description: I have the veer 4 wheel stroller. The brake on it just broke for the 3rd time and I'm on my 3rd warrantied stroller (all brake related issues). The brake on all their strollers is defective however they keep selling them. They need to fix the problem before a child gets hurt.
justification: The brake issue is recurring but no injury has been reported yet, indicating a potential hazard.

incident_description:
On June 6th my 13 year old daughter had back surgery (2 rods and 18 screws) (she was unable to move). I bought her a unicorn glow pet. I got back to her hospital room and installed the batteries. Within seconds she said "mom i smell a [REDACTED]". I told her no and walked back to her bed and saw the pillow pet smoking and was to hot to touch. I hurried and removed the batteries and the room reaked of melting wires and smoke. I contacted the company and all they wanna do is send her another one. If I had not been there with her she would have been burned or worse.
She was in [REDACTED] Hospital
justification: The incident involved a smoking and overheating toy, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says that he started smelling smoke.  His son walked into the room where the unit was plugged in and found it smoking and sparking.  Flames started shooting out of the small adapter from it and he placed it outside.  The consumer says the unit was plugged in for no more than 30 minutes prior to the incident.  This was the first time this unit had been plugged in for use.
justification: The incident involved smoke, sparks, and flames, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I noticed the CPSC has recalled an child's musical table toy by Battat, cited here:
http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml11/11342.html

I have a VERY similar toy, marketed by Boikido and still being sold on Amazon.com, that has experienced exactly the same issues - plastic pegs that could become a choking hazard. In my case they did not "loosen and detach" but snapped off under very light use.

See here:
http://www.amazon.com/Boikido-152278-Wooden-Percussion-Table/dp/B001B9E870/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1337782502&sr=8-1

I think this product should be considered for a similar recall.

Regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The plastic pegs can snap off and pose a choking hazard, which is an incident with no reported injury.

incident_description: I would like to report the Evenflo Pivot Modular Travel System With SafeMax Car Seat. After only a handful of uses the front wheel turns and the stroller makes a squeaky sound. When I put the car seat in the base, it only clicks on one side and if I do not push it all the way in, the car seat wont click into place. I didnt notice this until I heard a click after driving for thirty minutes and noticed that the car seat wasnt clicked into the base all the way. I then went to their website and read the reviews of people having the same issue. This product is unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: The stroller and car seat have functional issues, but no injury or incident was reported.

incident_description: I put batteries in the Glo Worm for the first time but it wouldn't do anything. The light came on once very briefly but that's it. I turned it off and went to get the manual in the other room to see if I was doing something wrong. When I got back, I smelled a burning plastic odor. I opened up the fabric shell and removed the white plastic part that holds the electronics. I felt something hot under my finger and that's when I noticed the plastic melting right above the button/microphone. Since the switch was off, I had to unscrew the door and remove the batteries to get it to stop (a screwdriver is required to access the battery compartment). I opened up the case to see what was going on and saw that the wires leading from the batteries had burned through their insulation and had begun to melt and burn the plastic case. If I hadn't noticed the burning smell and investigated, the whole thing could have melted or caught on fire and injured myself or my son.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toy that could have caused injury or fire, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description:
Caller's son received a light up stuffed dog for his first birthday around August 4th/

As she was putting her one year old son to bed on August 28th, 2012 she picked the dreamlite up to move it and the tail came off in her hand.

She believes that he may have chewed or pulled the tail however she and her husband also believe that he shouldn't have been able to disconnect any part of it.

They are reporting this incident as a choking hazard with the believe that it could happen to any child even one whose teeth have just come in as her son's have.

 They are vert concerned because if they hadn't noticed the tail being disconnected, their son would have definitely put it in his mouth at some point and most likely choked. 

They would like the public to be aware of this danger.
justification: The tail detached, posing a potential choking hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Ingestion of 4 bucky ball magnets. Patient presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain and distension, decreased oral intake and vomiting. The magnets were removed from the colon endoscopically.
justification: The patient suffered abdominal pain and required endoscopic removal, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The product,  paw patrol Halloween bucket, intended to be used by young children to collect Halloween candy. The child placed the bucket on head and it got stuck. It bruised and cut her face.
justification: The child suffered bruises and cuts, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We are returning our B. Toys Lets Flow Bowling set because one of the pins popped open and all the little balls came pouring out. Our almost-2-year-old immediately tried to pop them in his mouth. This is a serious issue that the company needs to address and probably warrants a recall. Of note, however, the large, glowing ball was misshapen. I mention this only because it is possible the toy incurred a heavy impact during packaging, in transit or at the store, which might explain both issues.
justification: The incident involved a toy malfunction that could have led to choking, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
6 year old and 3 year old were building structures with the Picasso tiles, when one of the tiles opened and released magnet pieces onto the floor.  The pieces could be snapped back together, only to reopen again.

The small magnetic pieces are choking hazards.
justification: The incident involves small magnetic pieces posing a choking hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I am a Pediatrician and a Child Passenger Safety Technician (CPST).   I saw a mom/baby during newborn nursery rounds that had a strange and alarming car seat.  The brand was "safeplus".  Mom says they got it on Amazon with a stroller too.  There were ZERO labels on the seat (no FMVSS 213, no use labels), no chest clip, and only two harness slot positions - the lower one of which didn't have a corresponding hole in the foam behind the fabric to allow it to be threaded.  The overall quality was poor.  

I googled it - and the descriptions on Kmart and Walmart's websites use language like "pram" and "pushchair" for stroller which sounds european to me.  

Here's a link:
http://www.kmart.com/safeplus-3-in1-foldable-baby-kids-travel-stroller/p-SPM15259796024?plpSellerId=factorydirectsale&prdNo=2&blockNo=2&blockType=G2

It is also sold at Walmart as: https://www.walmart.com/ip/Costway-3-In1-Foldable-Baby-Kids-Travel-Stroller-Newborn-Infant-Pushchair-Buggy-Black/911429142?wmlspartner=wlpa&selectedSellerId=1848&adid=22222222227081756922&wmlspartner=wmtlabs&wl0=&wl1=g&wl2=c&wl3=196328395184&wl4=pla-316597992715&wl5=9007908&wl6=&wl7=&wl8=&wl9=pla&wl10=113146030&wl11=online&wl12=911429142&wl13=&veh=sem

I also checked with senior officials at the Maryland Dept of Health who are CPST instructors and they agreed that this seat is not legal for use (or sale) in the U.S.
justification: The car seat is not legal for use or sale in the U.S. and poses a potential safety risk, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I bought Jangostor jumbo water beads from Amazon a year ago for my two year old. I found them after searching for sensory toys for toddlers on Amazon. At some point my son mustve swallowed one. We had no idea. One day he seemed lethargic and started vomiting. It took the ER two days to figure out what was wrong. They eventually did an ultrasound and found out that he was 100% obstructed. He ended up in the hospital for nearly a month and underwent 3 separate surgeries to remove the water bead and repair damage from the extensive surgery. These water beads are marketed as fun for all ages. This could not be FURTHER from the truth. These should not be marketed to children.
justification: The child suffered severe injuries requiring multiple surgeries and a month-long hospital stay due to swallowing a water bead.

incident_description: (02/11/2015) The consumer stated that there is a knob on the car that shifts it to forward or reverse. The consumer stated that her son got the ring finger on his right hand caught in the part of the shift gear that connects to the car. The tip of his finger was cut. No medical attention.
justification: The incident resulted in a finger injury (cut tip), but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
Hello !
Product - Contours Itsy Lightweight Stroller
In 4 months of use, the stroller folded by itself 4 times when our son was sitting there, despite the fact that it was assembled, it doesn't have a reliable fastening
This happened three times in a parking lot and once at the airport.
Twice I managed to catch it and twice my son hit his head
Thank you
justification: The stroller folded unexpectedly multiple times, resulting in the child hitting their head twice, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My daughter has (had) the seal glow pet. she was laying down resting when she noticed it smelt gross, this is when I discovered that the on switch was very hot to the touch and did smell of an electrical fire . I examined the on switch by cutting the fabric open and discovered that the switch had melted, brown marks on the wires. I am glad I caught it when we did and it did no harm to my child. if it would have gone un-noticed I fear that things could have been much worse.
justification: The incident involved a melted switch and potential electrical fire hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: My two year old child fell backwards from the stroller that I purchased on Amazon. She was just sitting and when she leaned to back the stroller fell and she hit the concrete floor.
justification: The child fell from the stroller and hit the concrete floor, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: A toy sold by Walmart  designed for 6 mth plus to stick to surface hit my 12 month baby in the face lacerated her lip and cracked her front tooth.
justification: The toy caused a laceration and cracked tooth, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 5 month old was playing with a Bright Starts Shake And Rattle Barbell, and he was able to shove one end of it into his mouth to where he couldn't get it out and could not breathe. Even I had a hard time getting it out of his mouth, but I had to hurry in order to prevent him from further suffocation. Once I was able to get it out, it had left a small cut on the inside of my son's lip. He was also VERY upset for quite some time. If I hadn't been just feet away from him, this very easily could have killed him!
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut on the child's lip and significant distress, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests such incidents could happen if not closely monitored, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: I was pushing the baby stroller taking a walk with my infant. The stroller is a Pram like stroller (bassinet). I went to cross the street (busy main road in our town) it is a slight bend so I pushed the stroller slightly to the left to get down the sidewalk ramp then went to swiftly cross the street. The front 2 wheels of the stroller got stuck sideways making the stroller unable to move forward and the force of me pushing tipped the stroller forward. Jolting the baby and causeing me to trip  on the back as I moved to the left to grab the front of the stroller. Which also left me with scrapes and abrasions to my right leg. Had I not buckled the baby in she would of fallen out onto the street with some force. I then turned around to walk home and the wheels locked another 3 times in which I had to stop walking to fix them forward. I went online to check reviews of the product to see if mine was faulty and alas there were pages of reviews that the same thing was happening to others. The reviews said they contacted the manufacturer, I even sent them a message with no response. I checked to see if a recall was issued and it was not. A child could easily be thrown from the stroller due to the faulty wheels, the person pushing could also trip over/ or even fall over the stroller once tipped. When the wheels lock up the stroller comes to an abrupt and forceful stop. You then have to adjust the wheels every time which when pushing a stroller you have to stop to adjust them that may leave the operator and child in a potentially dangerous situation such as the middle of the street, parking lot etc.
justification: The incident caused scrapes and abrasions to the parent and could have resulted in the infant being thrown from the stroller, indicating a potential for injury.

incident_description:
I bought these plastic magnetic gears for my 4 y/o daughter late 2011. This past week, she brought me one of the gears, and the peg/screw that holds the magnet into the gear had come out, and so had the magnet.  It appears that the base has lightly cracked, allowing the screw to loosen.  The base has appeared to start cracking on at least one other of these gears.  I found the product online- Oliblock OliGear.  I attempted to phone both numbers listed, with no answer- the email address given has bounced back as undeliverable.   My daughter was not hurt luckily, but I cannot get a hold of the company regarding this defect.  I don't want similar to occur to other families that might be worse.  

-[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a product defect with no injury reported, and the company is uncontactable, indicating potential for recurrence.

incident_description: Toy dog shaped guitar brand name appears to be called strum. Strap became tangled around my 2 1/2 year old granddaughters neck.. the weight of the guitar made it impossible for her to untangle herself. I was there and was able to unwrap the strap from her neck. I took photos of her neck and the toy
justification: The strap became tangled around the child's neck, posing a choking hazard, but no injury was reported as the situation was resolved in time.

incident_description: Placed our daughter in her GB Qbit Stroller, buckled her in, turned away and the stroller collapsed on her. Mild bump on the head but mostly just upset as she was frightened.  Looked up the product online and found out that it had been recalled. We will not be using this stroller any more.
justification: The stroller collapsed on the child, causing a mild bump on the head and distress, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Hi my children have been using the graco double stroller and while sitting on the bottom of the double stroller the stroller seat unclicks and he has hit his head and face multiple times on the concrete. Very dangerous.
justification: The child hit his head and face multiple times on concrete, indicating injury.

incident_description: My husband was pushing my Two year old daughter in the UPPAbaby Vista stroller. She was sitting in and strapped into the Rumble Seat (model number 0101, manufacture date Aug. 2014). The stroller hit a bump in the sidewalk and the Rumble Seat adapters detached from the stroller, ejecting the seat holding my daughter. She landed face first onto the sidewalk. Her forehead split open in two places and we had to take her to the emergency room where she got ten stitches. She also got surface scrapes on both wrists, one knee, and one toe. Five weeks later (today) she has large scars on her forehead where the stitches were.
justification: The child suffered injuries requiring emergency room treatment and stitches, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: My son received a Thomas and Friends hat and belt (value pack - Gullane (Thomas) Limited) as a gift. He put the belt around his neck and tightened it - it does not have an easy release - my husband had difficulty getting it off, but finally managed. Left marks on my son's neck, he was very frightened, having trouble breathing while around his neck. We were very fortunate that he was in the room with us when it happened.
justification: The child experienced trouble breathing and had marks on his neck, indicating physical injury and distress.

incident_description: Using provided tools to find gem hidden in Dig It Gold product, the sandy surface flew through air and embedded in eye causing multiple corneal abrasions.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple corneal abrasions, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: My son, 3 years and 7 months old was playing with and Empire Siren Wistle. It is a plastic tube approximately 4" long with two wheels inside that make a "whizzing" sound when you blow into it.  He discovered that it makes a noise both when you exhale and when you inhale through the tube.  On an inhale, one of the small wheels flew into his mouth and he swallowed it.  It is about the size of a dime, but 3x thicker. After approximately 20 minutes of complaining of chest pain, we realized that it had probably lodged in his esophagus.  We went to the ER where they took Xrays.  After about an hour, the pain subsided and we were advised by the ER Doctor, an ENT, and a surgeon that it had probably dislodged and we would find it at the other end some time in the next few days. We are waiting...
justification: The child swallowed a small object, experienced chest pain, and required medical evaluation, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the child's age and the toy's design.

incident_description:
Two babies were strapped into "baby trend exposition double jogger" and the sitter locked back wheels at the top of her driveway.  She started to walk into her garage and stroller became unlocked on one wheel then moved backwards down her driveway, spun around (as one wheel was still locked).  This movement unlocked the other wheel and stroller rolled backward off driveway and started to flip over.  As the babies were about to hit the ground face first, the sitter was able to catch the back wheel that was in the arm and pull stroller back down to ground before it hit the ground.

The 15month old suffered a left broken humerus.  The 7month old suffered bruising on inside leg.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken humerus for one baby and bruising for the other, which qualifies as injury (severity level 3). The scenario involves a common stroller mishap, making it likely to occur again under similar conditions (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
DANGEROUS TOY!!  This is in regards to the Haba Geo Shape Tack Zap (http://www.habausa.com/geo-shape-tack-zap.html).

My 4-year-old son swallowed one of the nails in this toy at his Montessori daycare.  The nails are small and sharp and this is NOT an age appropriate toy for 4-year-olds.   Children obviously put small parts in their mouths, and these nails are too dangerous for the risk.
justification: A 4-year-old swallowed a small, sharp nail from the toy, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description:
I sent this to Uppababy customer service on 10-24-20 // 
I am writing today to report a major stroller accident that occurred because the Uppababy Vista broke while my child was strapped into the Toddler seat. I am still shaken up and extremely upset that after investing in such an expensive product, which we did because it would bring us the peace of mind knowing our kids would be safe, broke on us and injured my son.

Friday evening, my husband had just loaded my 21 month old into the top toddler seat. He started to roll the stroller backward, preparing to turn the stroller and position it to leave our front entry. As he pulled the stroller back, the Toddler seat snapped and my son and the seat fell sideways into the basket and then bounced out and landed on the concrete. He got a swollen lip and was bleeding in his mouth. He now has a small chip on his front tooth too. 

We were moving the stroller back. The front rumble seat wasnt attached and therefore my petite 3 year old wasnt in the front location. My son who fell is 30 lbs, meaning he is 20lbs under the weight limit for the Toddler Seat! No stairs were involved. 

How could this happen? Do you have known structural integrity issues with the Jake model? 

Im not sure how you will find us on record, but here is some information: 
We have an Uppababy Vista (Jake) purchased at Nordstrom. We have also purchased all of the adapters, the [REDACTED] carseat, extra carseat base, inserts for seats, and [REDACTED]. I attend the annual official Uppababy Tune-Ups. In the past, I have reported that my wheels were shaking as I walk. They cleaned them, and we continue to clean them at home. But the shaking still occurs and makes the ride/push challenging to walk straight. Should this have been a sign that our particular unit has integrity issues? I assume your Tune Up staff report everything that I have said was an issue, so this should be on file from two separate Tune Up events. 

We store our Vista in the garage where it doesnt have direct access to weather and we live in San Diego which is a very mild climate even while the stroller is in use. Again, how can this seat piece just snap off? 

I am not comfortable using our stroller again, nor do I think its even possible based on how the seat broke off. I would like to speak to someone to resolve this immediately because I travel with my kids on a road trip in two weeks. 

Thank,
[REDACTED]

SERIAL # VIS0616010144402
justification: The child suffered a swollen lip, bleeding in the mouth, and a chipped tooth, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I purchased the "3D Kinetic Spring" for my 8-year-old child at approximately 6pm on Friday, July, 27th. Within 2 hours of purchasing it, we had to cut and remove it from around his neck. My husband and I were in the front seats of our vehicle, driving, and heard stifled wimpering. We turned to see the "toy" compressing his neck. Fortunately, we were in town and quickly thinking, my husband ran across the street to purchase wire cutters (we have the package and receipt). I was able to wedge my fingers between the coils and his neck and relieve some of the pressure. I also photographed the situation as we waited. It was a terrifying ordeal... the "what if's" still haunt me. The toy is presented as being versatile on the package. He saw the image of the toy as a "bracelet" and thought it could also be a necklace. We are worried that other children will get hurt or strangled. There are many variations of this product available from different manufacturers.
justification: The child's neck was compressed by the toy, posing a serious risk of injury or strangulation, though no actual injury was reported.
